article.articleHeadline: Strengthening the Bundibugyo virus disease response through community evidence
article.articleSummary: USD 3 million from Wellcome will strengthen Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) by integrating community-generated evidence with epidemiological, clinical and laboratory data. With no specific medical countermeasures for BVD, understanding community perceptions, care-seeking behavior and barriers to public-health measures is critical to limiting transmission. The funding expands rapid assessments for community protection—an interagency method delivering real-time social and behavioural insights to guide operations. Developed with UNICEF, IFRC and Africa CDC, the approach has informed mpox, Ebola and cholera responses and generated evidence for more than 8.8 million people. Since the May 17, 2026 PHEIC declaration, WHO and DRC authorities have used findings to improve community surveillance, toll-free hotlines, psychosocial support for frontline workers, and timely lab-result communications; ambulance delays and treatment-centre capacity are being addressed. Dr Nina Gobat leads; Wellcome’s Natsuko Imai champions rapid, practice-ready analytics.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chengalpattu: Increase in dengue fever transmission among children - public concern.
article.articleSummary: On 16 August 2026, dengue fever is spreading among children in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, with cases reported from Vinayakapuram in Keerapakkam panchayat. Several children have been hospitalized for dengue, and parents as well as the public express concern as transmission among youngsters appears to be accelerating. The public is calling on the government to speed up dengue prevention and control activities. The report gives no specific case counts or fatalities, and provides no details on laboratory confirmation, infection sources, or whether cases are imported or exported. No additional clinical information or outbreak timeline is provided. The piece highlights public health demand for intensified vector-control measures to curb pediatric dengue transmission in the area.

article.articleHeadline: 大陸7月新增新冠確診52.2萬例 較6月暴增5.6倍
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mainland China reports 522,000 new COVID-19 cases in July, up 5.6-fold from June.
article.articleSummary: Mainland China reports 522,000 new COVID-19 cases in July, up 5.6-fold from June, per the China CDC, spanning 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps. July's severe cases rose to 487 from 130 in June, while deaths remained at 1. The infection has been downgraded to Class B, with focus on treatment and protection in key venues; COVID-19 is now a common, seasonal respiratory disease with about 1–2 waves per year. The current wave’s rise has slowed and sits at the high plateau of this cycle; elderly and those with chronic diseases remain high-risk, though antiviral therapies are effective. In the week of Aug 3–9, among 216 sentinel hospitals, SARS-CoV-2 positivity was 21.1% in outpatient/ER influenza-like illness samples (down 1.1 pp) and 8.6% in hospitalized severe acute respiratory infection samples (up 0.1 pp).

article.articleHeadline: Five graphs show Ebola outbreak on track to be worst in history
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in north‑east Ituri province with Bunia as its capital, is on track to be the deadliest on record. Friday, 2,214 deaths from 4,727 confirmed infections, 85% in Ituri. The outbreak is accelerating faster than any prior, reaching 250 deaths in 37 days and 1,000 confirmed cases in 38 days, versus 2014–2016 West Africa. The epidemic likely began two to three months before the May 15 declaration, with February misdiagnoses of malaria/typhoid later attributed to Ebola. About 80% of July cases could not be linked to known contacts, indicating hidden community transmission. Most deaths occur in the community, not treatment centers, amid unsafe handling of bodies. Testing delays stem from Bundibugyo virus shortages and kits that initially detected only the Zaire strain, with reagent shortages delaying diagnoses. Health workers are underpaid, under-protected, and strikes hinder response; Uganda has detected exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: AI Ciptakan Virus Penghancur Bakteri yang Resisten Terhadap Obat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: AI Creates Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteriophage
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria face a potential new ally as artificial intelligence designs bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—enabling lab-produced candidates. A Science-published study by researchers from Stanford University and the Arc Institute in the United States tested 285 AI-designed phage genomes, yielding 16 functional bacteriophages capable of replicating and targeting Escherichia coli. By combining several phages, the team attacked bacteria that had developed resistance to original phages. Israel’s Hadassah Medical Center infectious disease expert Ran Nir-Paz, director of the Israel Phage Therapy Center, notes AI processes genetic information similarly to language models; Evo 1 and Evo 2 were trained on large genetic datasets to learn the DNA/RNA language, enabling new sequences. Implications for antibiotic resistance are significant, though biosafety concerns persist. Dateline Jakarta, 2026-08-16.

triage.notes: 本記事は米国・イスラエルの研究者によるAI創薬（ファージ療法）研究の科学ニュースであり、インドネシア(ジャカルタ)は単なる配信地であり実際の疾病発生地ではない。感染症イベントではないため対象国に該当なし。

article.articleHeadline: CAG flags E. coli in drinking water at railway stations, finds widespread amenity lapses
article.articleSummary: Comptroller and Auditor General flagged drinking-water quality at Indian Railways, finding E. coli and other bacteria in water cooler samples at eight stations across four zones: Southern Railway (Coimbatore, Palakkad Junction), South Central (Hyderabad); Central Railway (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala); Eastern Railway (Madhupur). Tests of taps on platforms at 49 stations across eight zones in 2022-23 and 56 stations across nine zones in 2023-24 showed presence of Total coliforms including E. coli. Some E. coli strains can cause food poisoning, diarrhoea, and, in severe cases, kidney failure. The audit also found bacteriological testing unsatisfactory at eight stations across four zones in 2022-23 and 11 stations across five zones in 2023-24. The report covers audits from 2019-20 through 2023-24, including unreported cases identified after 2023-24.

article.articleHeadline: CAG Flags E. Coli In Drinking Water Across Railway Stations; Zones Flout Board Norms
article.articleSummary: E. coli-contaminated drinking water was detected at multiple Indian Railways stations in a CAG audit. Bacteriological testing was not conducted at 59 of 512 non-suburban stations. Water cooler samples tested positive for E. coli at Coimbatore and Palakkad Junctions (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala (Central Railway); and Madhupur (Eastern Railway). Tests for total coliforms, including E. coli, were found in taps at 49 stations (2022-23) across eight zones and 56 stations (2023-24) across nine zones; eight stations (2022-23) and 11 stations (2023-24) showed unsatisfactory bacteriological parameters beyond coliforms. The audit spans 2019-20 to 2023-24; scale: 5,908 non-suburban stations, 7,424 daily trains, 292.4 crore passengers (2023-24). Recommendations urge end-to-end water testing and strict enforcement of Minimum Essential Amenities under the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol.

article.articleHeadline: CAG flags E. coli bacteria in drinking water at Railway stations, cites violation of Railway Board norms
article.articleSummary: Comptroller and Auditor General findings: E. coli was detected in drinking water from coolers at several railway stations, including Coimbatore and Palakkad Junctions (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala (Central Railway); and Madhupur (Eastern Railway). Coliforms were found in taps at 49 stations (2022-23) and 56 stations (2023-24) across eight and nine zones. Bacteriological tests beyond total coliforms were unsatisfactory at eight stations (2022-23) and 11 stations (2023-24). The audit, covering 2019-20 to 2023-24 at 512 NSG stations, found MEAs deficient at 458 stations (over 89%). Railway Board’s April 2018 guidelines mandated MEAs by Aug 31, 2018, including drinking water, latrines, and seating. Even NSG-1 stations such as CSMT, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi, and Mumbai Central showed gaps in seating, sanitary facilities, and dustbins. Recommended strict testing under the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol. E. coli can cause diarrhoea and kidney failure.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola 50 años después: lecciones que serán cruciales para prevenir futuras epidemias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola 50 Years Later: Lessons That Will Be Crucial for Preventing Future Epidemics
article.articleSummary: Ebola, first identified in 1976 near the Ebola River in Zaire (now the Democratic Republic of the Congo), has caused dozens of outbreaks, including the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that killed over 11,000 and revealed health-system weaknesses. Fifty years of progress include effective vaccines and monoclonal antibody treatments, plus faster diagnostics, but outcomes hinge on time: early case finding, isolation, contact tracing, and community engagement. In May 2026, outbreaks were confirmed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, involving the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, for which no vaccine or specific treatment exists yet, with candidates under evaluation. WHO is bolstering surveillance, cross-border preparedness, clinical management, supplies, and community involvement amid humanitarian crises, insecurity, and high population movement. Transparent communication and cultural respect are essential; not all Ebolavirus strains respond identically. Lessons also inform COVID-19 responses, including genomic sequencing and international cooperation.

article.articleHeadline: चेंगलपट्टू जिले में डेंगू का डर, बच्चे अस्पताल में भर्ती
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue scare in Chengalpattu district; children admitted to hospital.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever concerns in Vinayagapuram, Keerappakkam panchayat, Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, with several fever patients admitted to government hospitals in Guduvanchery, Chengalpattu and nearby areas. Official dengue case counts have not yet been confirmed. Local residents report fever, headache, vomiting and weakness across age groups, fueling fears of wider transmission beyond children. Parents urge swift public health action to protect schoolchildren, including medical camps in Vinayagapuram, screening of symptomatic individuals, and prompt hospital referrals for those needing care. Calls for intensified vector-control measures—fogging and elimination of standing water around streets, drains, and homes—and house-to-house surveys to identify breeding sites. Community requests reliable medicine, testing, and staff at nearby health centers, plus public awareness campaigns on dengue symptoms and precautions and adherence to medical guidance rather than self-medication. Officials should treat this as a public health priority.

article.articleHeadline: Bệnh sốt xuất huyết: Hết sốt không phải hết bệnh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever: Fever subsides, but the illness is not over.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is surging in the Mekong Delta region of southwestern Vietnam during the rainy season. In Can Tho City, the Children's Hospital reports over 1,500 dengue admissions this year, with more than 70 severe cases, up 183% from the same period. Across Can Tho, total dengue cases exceed 3,000 since the start of 2026. Dengue typically progresses in three stages; the critical second stage occurs around days 3–7, when fever may subside but plasma leakage, shock and other severe complications can develop. Parents should closely monitor for lethargy, irritability, cold limbs, severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood, or reduced urination, and seek care if fever persists or tests are needed on day 2. Do not self-medicate with aspirin or ibuprofen, nor antibiotics, and avoid home IV fluids. Vaccination is supplementary; emphasis on environmental hygiene and mosquito control. Can Tho marked ASEAN Dengue Prevention Day on June 15.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo worsens, long transmission warned
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak worsens with 4,727 confirmed cases and 2,214 deaths across 55 health zones in Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo; Ituri remains the epicenter. Buta health zone in Bas-Uele is newly affected after a traveler from Isiro in Haut-Uele went to Buta and died there. So far, 976 people have recovered. Persistent community transmission and gaps in contact tracing threaten containment. Contact follow-up rate is 82.6%, but Africa CDC cautions that this metric does not reflect unidentified contacts. WHO notes most deaths occur in communities and many new cases are not on existing contact lists, indicating untracked transmission chains. The outbreak is moving faster than any prior Ebola outbreak and could eclipse the West Africa 2014-2016 epidemic (over 28,600 cases).

article.articleHeadline: Bicol records ASF cases
article.articleSummary: ASF in the Bicol region of the Philippines is being addressed with depopulation, surveillance, and monitoring across affected barangays. LGUs are urged to enforce border controls and restrict hog movement as DA Bicol, the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), and the National Meat Inspection Service (NMIS) coordinate strict biosecurity, sanitation, and disinfection of swine farms. Residents are advised to disregard fake news and follow official announcements from DA Bicol. ASF is a highly contagious viral disease affecting domestic and wild pigs, with mortality up to 100%; it does not affect humans but devastates food security, local agriculture, and pork industries. The Philippines’ 2026 strategy emphasizes targeted localized containment, strict border controls, and a push for a commercial vaccine rollout. Nationwide, affected barangays have decreased, but sporadic provincial outbreaks continue to trigger localized restrictions and heightened biosecurity.

triage.headline_ja: ビコール地方でASF（アフリカ豚熱）症例を記録

E. coli strains can cause food poisoning, diarrhoea, and kidney failure. The findings expose potential health risks to travelers and indicate gaps in water safety and sanitation at major rail hubs. The report relies on laboratory-confirmed contamination data collected during the audit and identifies drinking-water sources as the likely infection route. The article does not describe an active outbreak or documented cases tied to these stations, and there is no detail on remediation actions or timelines.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Butembo : Mgr Sikuli appelle les familles à la responsabilité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Butembo: Bishop Sikuli urges families to take responsibility.
article.articleSummary: As of August 16, 2026, Ebola in Butembo, the epicenter of the outbreak in North Kivu, is being fueled by families who retrieve and handle bodies suspected of dying from Ebola before safe-burial teams arrive. This high-risk practice could further spread the virus within households and the broader community. Monseigneur Melchisédech Sikuli Paluku, bishop of the Butembo-Beni diocese, calls on families to act responsibly and avoid unsafe handling that could kill or infect others. Health responders report resistance to secure burial operations, raising concern that improper corpse handling could reignite transmission chains. The article underscores the need for strict adherence to safe-burial protocols to prevent additional cases and ongoing community transmission.

triage.headline_ja: ブテンボのエボラ：シクリ司教が家族に責任ある行動を呼びかけ

article.articleHeadline: الأمم المتحدة: إيبولا يودي بحياة شخص كل 30 دقيقة في الكونغو

Fletcher urged the international community to intensify efforts to curb transmission. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with the Saturday update dated around 15 August 2026 providing the numbers cited.

article.articleSummary: E. coli bacteria detected in drinking water at eight Indian Railways stations: Coimbatore and Palakkad Junction (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); four Central Railway stations—Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala—and Madhupur (Eastern Railway). article.articleHeadline: 逾八成肝癌由乙肝病毒引起！专家提醒_央广网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 80% of liver cancers are caused by hepatitis B virus! Experts remind - CNR.net
article.articleSummary: China’s liver cancer burden is driven by hepatitis B virus (HBV), which causes more than 80% of cases. Lin Bingliang, Infectious Diseases chief at Sun Yat-sen University Third Hospital, notes vaccination as the most effective, lowest-cost prevention. Despite vaccination expansion and mother-to-child transmission control, many infections remain undiagnosed or untreated, leaving cirrhosis and cancer risks high. China records about 400,000 new liver cancer cases annually, with a 5-year survival around 14.1%. The five major viral hepatitis types are HAV, HEV (food/waterborne) and HBV, HDV, HCV (blood and perinatal/sexual). Guangdong launched an early hepatitis prevention and treatment program in 2023 with 280 million yuan, screening 20–70-year-olds across 57 counties and aiming for ≥70% HBV screening; nearly 10 million screened, about 8 per 100 HBsAg-positive. Since 2018, Sun Yat-sen’s chronic HBV cure project enrolled >30,000 patients, with >10,000 achieving clinical cure, and new HBV drugs nearing clinical use. Clinics were held in Guangzhou (Tianhe, Lingnan), Zhaoqing, East Guangdong, and Tibet’s Chaya County, with online livestreams.

triage.headline_ja: 肝がんの8割以上がB型肝炎ウイルス由来！専門家が注意喚起 - 央広網

article.articleHeadline: 暑期野游慎防蚊虫 疾控专家提醒：要防护到位
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Summer outdoor activities: beware mosquitoes and insects; disease-control experts remind you to stay properly protected.
article.articleSummary: Summer outdoor activities raise infection risks in China’s warm, wet environments. Leptospirosis, caused by Leptospira bacteria, thrives in fresh water after heavy rain and floods—waters in mountain streams, ponds, ditches, and rice paddies contaminated by animal urine (rats, pigs). Seawater poses lower risk. Key symptoms: sudden high fever, severe calf muscle pain, red conjunctiva, swollen lymph nodes; seek prompt medical care if exposure occurred and disclose outdoor water activity. Avoid self-medicating with NSAIDs or antibiotics before diagnosis to prevent complications. Dengue fever risk persists in areas with Aedes albopictus; watch for fever with joint pain and rash and avoid high-outbreak regions. For camping, wear long sleeves/pants and closed shoes, camp in open, ventilated areas, and be vigilant for mosquitoes, biting midges, and snakes. Inform physicians about outdoor exposure to enable early diagnosis and treatment.

triage.headline_ja: 夏の野外活動は蚊や虫に注意を—疾病対策専門家が適切な防護を呼びかけ

article.articleHeadline: Trẻ 2 tháng tuổi mắc giang mai bẩm sinh, dễ nhầm bệnh ngoài da
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A 2-month-old infant with congenital syphilis, easily mistaken for a skin disease.
article.articleSummary: Two-month-old girl in Quang Tri Province presented with a widespread red, dry, peeling rash on the palms and soles, nasal discharge, slightly yellowish skin, pale mucosa, abdominal distension, and enlarged liver and spleen. Diagnosed with early congenital syphilis transmitted from an untreated mother who had tested positive for syphilis. Early congenital syphilis can mimic common pediatric dermatoses, underscoring the need for professional evaluation rather than home remedies. The infant received 10 days of targeted intravenous antibiotics, with gradual improvement in skin lesions and overall health during admission at Quang Tri Provincial General Hospital. The report emphasizes routine prenatal syphilis screening and timely maternal treatment to prevent vertical transmission. Parents are urged to seek medical care promptly for neonates with abnormal rashes, especially on hands and feet, and not to self-medicate.

article.articleHeadline: E. Coli Detected: CAG Flags Contaminated Drinking Water Across Railway Stations
article.articleSummary: Eight railway stations across four zones showed E. coli in drinking water from water coolers: Coimbatore and Palakkad Junction (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala (Central Railway); Madhupur (Eastern Railway). The CAG audit of 512 non-suburban stations found 49 stations across eight zones with total coliforms in taps in 2022-23, and 56 stations across nine zones in 2023-24. Residual chlorine testing was not carried out at 78 stations across 13 zones. MEA compliance was lacking at 458 of 512 stations. Shortages included latrines at 201 stations, urinals at 403 stations, and water taps at 2,035 stations. Recommendations: strengthen sanitation and garbage management; tighten water-supply inspections and comprehensive drinking water testing; link contractor payments/penalties to sanitation outcomes; implement station-wise action plans with timelines. diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: എച്ച്1 എൻ1-ന് ശേഷം നിങ്ങൾക്ക് ബ്രെയിൻ ഫോഗ് അനുഭവപ്പെടാം; കാരണമിതാ... | You may experience brain fog after H1N1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: You may experience brain fog after H1N1; what is the reason...
article.articleSummary: Double influenza cases in Kerala, India, indicate a rising H1N1 outbreak. This year, influenza infections have doubled compared with last year. Even after recovery, many patients report brain fog—fatigue, difficulty concentrating, slowed thinking, and memory lapses that can last days to weeks. Brain fog arises from the inflammatory response during infection, sleep disruption, dehydration, and nutritional shortfalls; it is more noticeable in severe H1N1 cases with oxygen drop or hospitalization but does not signify permanent brain damage. Recovery centers on adequate sleep, hydration, balanced nutrition, and a gradual return to activities while avoiding excessive mental or physical stress; some medications may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Most people improve as post-illness fatigue eases. If symptoms persist or worsen, especially with speech problems, severe headaches, fainting, confusion, or limb weakness, seek urgent medical care. There is no fixed duration; weeks-long recovery can occur.

article.articleHeadline: Do You Drink Water At Railway Stations? CAG Flags E. Coli At These 8 Locations
article.articleSummary: Eight railway stations across four zones reported drinking-water samples from coolers testing positive for E. coli: Coimbatore and Palakkad Junction (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala (Central Railway); Madhupur (Eastern Railway). E. coli indicates possible faecal contamination and unsafe drinking water. Across taps, total coliform bacteria (including E. coli) were found at 49 stations in 2022-23 and 56 stations in 2023-24 across eight and nine zones, with eight and eleven stations respectively showing bacteriological testing beyond total coliforms being unsatisfactory. Bacteriological analysis was not conducted at 59 stations across six zones. In total, 512 stations surveyed; 458 (89%) deficient in minimum essential amenities, with latrines lacking at 201, urinals at 403, and drinking-water taps at 2,035 stations. Deficiencies include CSMT, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi, and Mumbai Central. Railways urged to follow the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol and complete testing.

article.articleHeadline: E. coli bacteria found in drinking water samples across railway stations: CAG report
article.articleSummary: E. coli detected in drinking water samples from water coolers at eight Indian Railway stations across four zones (Coimbatore and Palakkad Junctions in Southern Railway; Hyderabad in South Central Railway; Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala in Central Railway; Madhupur in Eastern Railway). Some strains can cause food poisoning, diarrhoea and kidney failure. The CAG audited 512 non-suburban stations; 458 (over 89%) were deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities (MEA). RB’s April 2018 directives mandated MEA, Recommended Amenities (RA), and Desirable Amenities (DA) across NSG 1–6, with MEA to be provided by 31 August 2018. Shortfalls noted at NSG-1 stations such as CSMT, Mumbai Central, Howrah, Sealdah, and New Delhi, including seating, sanitary facilities, dustbins, and electronic train indicators; latrines at 201 stations, urinals at 403, water taps at 2,035. The Railway Board should ensure inspection protocols and comprehensive water quality testing under the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol to mitigate health risks from contaminated water.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United Nations: "Ebola" is taking the life of one person every 30 minutes in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is accelerating, say United Nations and World Health Organization. Latest figures from the Congolese Ministry of Information report 4727 infections and 2214 deaths, yielding a case fatality rate of 46.8%. Officials warn that a death occurs about every 30 minutes, underscoring the urgent need for scaled-up international response, vaccination campaigns, and stronger surveillance. The article notes the expansion from an initial focus in Ituri to a wide geographic footprint, highlighting ongoing challenges in containment and resources.

article.articleHeadline: क्या फिर लौट रहा है CORONA? चीन में एक महीने में सामने आए 5 लाख से ज्यादा मामले, एक की मौत
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is the coronavirus making a comeback? Over 500,000 cases reported in China in one month, one death.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in China surged in July to about 522,000 new cases, with 487 severe cases and 1 death. The Chinese CDC frames this as a regular cyclical wave; cases are near a peak and entering a plateau, with August likely to see a decline. All tested samples identified the Omicron NB.1.8.1 lineage and sublineages. Beijing YouAn Hospital (Capital Medical University) respiratory specialist Li Tongzeng attributed factors to waning population immunity, ongoing SARS-CoV-2 mutation reducing antibody protection, and summer travel, with no evidence of increased virulence. Sentinel data from 1,041 hospitals show influenza-like illness around 4.3–4.5% of visits (late June–early August), with rising COVID-19 positivity among ILI patients. Most infections are mild; pneumonia and hospitalizations are rare. Since reclassifying COVID-19 as a Category B infectious disease, China experiences recurring seasonal waves. Preventive guidance includes vaccination, masks when needed, hygiene, and healthy living.

triage.headline_ja: コロナウイルスが再び流行の兆し？中国で1か月に50万人以上の感染確認、1人死亡
triage.triage_reason: 中国CDCは季節性の周期的な波と説明しており、重症例・死亡は極めて少なく、変異株の病原性増加の証拠もないため、異常性・深刻性ともに低いと判断される。
triage.notes: 中国CDCは本事象を通常の季節性流行（Category B感染症としての周期的波）と位置づけており、重症化率・死亡率ともに低い。オミクロンNB.1.8.1系統が検出されているが病原性増加の証拠はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola provoca la muerte de una persona cada 30 minutos en República Democrática del Congo, según la ONU
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola causes the death of one person every 30 minutes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to the UN.
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, Ebola is causing the death of roughly one person every 30 minutes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to the United Nations. The UN plans to deploy 20 team members to aid containment and medical care for the affected population. In a call for intensified response, Fletcher said that the number of teams ensuring safe and dignified burials must be doubled, treatment capacity tripled, contact tracing improved, and more experienced supervisors deployed. The appeal also highlights urgent needs for water, hygiene supplies, medical care, and other basic services in the region to curb transmission and support affected communities amid ongoing outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 国連によると、コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱により30分に1人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱による高い死亡率と国連による緊急対応要請があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 国連(UN)が国際支援チームの派遣を計画しており、埋葬・治療・接触者追跡体制の強化が急務とされている。致死率の高さと感染拡大の継続性から早急なリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: تحذيرات أممية من تسارع تفشي فيروس إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UN warns of accelerating Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: On 16 August 2026, the United Nations and the World Health Organization warn that the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating. As of 16 August 2026, the DRC reports 4,727 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,214 deaths, a case-fatality rate of about 46.8%. The outbreak is the largest and fastest-spreading on record for the country, expanding to 54 health zones across six provinces after initially being confined to the Mongababo area in Ituri province. UN humanitarian chief and WHO officials urge a strengthened international response, including enhanced surveillance, isolation, treatment, and community support to curb transmission. The report does not specify a single infection source or any imported/exported cases; emphasis remains on containment and sustained humanitarian aid to affected communities.

triage.headline_ja: 国連、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラウイルス流行加速に警鐘
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模・急速拡大中のエボラ流行(症例4,727件、致死率約46.8%)が6州54保健区に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 国連・WHOが国際的な支援強化を要請しており、過去最大規模の流行として緊急性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يفتك بالكونغو الديمقراطية بمعدل وفاة كل 30 دقيقة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo at a rate of one death every 30 minutes.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating at an unprecedented pace. The United Nations reports 2,128 deaths among more than 4,500 cases since its emergence in May. The situation is spreading rapidly, with the headline noting a death roughly every 30 minutes. International agencies urge urgent action, including expanding treatment centers, intensifying contact tracing, ensuring safe burials, and strengthening water and health services to curb transmission. Officials warn the outbreak could spill into adjacent provinces and neighboring countries. The UN calls for intensified international support and coordination to stop transmission, boost community engagement, improve infection prevention and control, and accelerate laboratory confirmation and case management, as of 16 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で猛威、30分に1人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の急速な拡大と高い致死数（4,500例中2,128死亡）が報告され、周辺国への波及懸念と国際支援要請があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 国連が国際的な支援強化と近隣国への拡大警戒を呼びかけており、致死率・拡大速度ともに深刻。続報でのケース数・地理的拡大状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: CAG Flags Gaps at Major Railway Stations: E. coli in Water, Poor Toilets and Missing Basic Amenities
article.articleSummary: E. coli detected in drinking water at 49 stations across eight zones in 2022-23 and 56 stations across nine zones in 2023-24, indicating faecal contamination risks at major Indian Railways stations such as Coimbatore, Palakkad, Hyderabad, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala and Madhupur. E. coli presence can cause diarrhoea and gastrointestinal infections. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) audit of 512 non-suburban stations found 458 stations (about 89–90%) deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities (MEA), including drinking water, waiting halls, seating, platform shelters, toilets, dustbins, and public-address systems. Even NSG-1 hubs like Mumbai Central, CSMT, Howrah, Sealdah and New Delhi showed shortcomings in seating and sanitary facilities. The report calls for stricter water-quality monitoring and full compliance with the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol to address safety and facilities at rail stations.

triage.headline_ja: CAGがインド主要鉄道駅の不備を指摘：飲料水から大腸菌検出、トイレ不備・基本設備の欠如
triage.triage_reason: 監査報告に基づくインフラ・衛生上の課題指摘であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクや症例報告ではないため、感染症シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 本記事はCAG（インド会計検査院）による鉄道駅の設備監査報告であり、大腸菌検出は水質検査結果としての言及にとどまる。具体的な感染症患者の発生や健康被害の報告はなく、感染症イベントとしてのシグナルではない。

article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, India, with several children admitted to government hospitals in Guduvanchery and Chengalpattu. The fever is also spreading among adults, presenting with symptoms such as headache and vomiting. No exact case or death counts are provided. Public concern rises as residents urge the Tamil Nadu government and panchayat administration to curb the outbreak. The report, citing Daily Thanthi, notes hospital admissions and calls for public health action, but offers no laboratory confirmation or infection source details. Published 2026-08-16.

triage.notes: デング熱はインドの当該地域で季節的に流行する疾患であり、検査確定症例数・死亡者数など詳細情報が不足しているため、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: E. coli bacteria found in drinking water at railway stations: CAG report
article.articleSummary: E. coli bacteria detected in drinking water samples from water coolers at eight railway stations across four zones, per a Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report surveying 512 non-suburban stations. Positive samples were found at Coimbatore and Palakkad Junction (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan and Lonavala (Central Railway); and Madhupur (Eastern Railway). Some E. coli strains can cause food poisoning, diarrhoea and kidney failure. The audit also found that 458 of 512 stations (over 89%) were deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities (MEA), including drinking water, waiting areas, sanitation facilities and information systems. The Railway Board had mandated MEA provision by 31 August 2018, with MEAs to be provided first at all stations. Deficiencies were noted even at NSG-1 hubs such as CSMT, Mumbai Central, Howrah, Sealdah and New Delhi.

triage.notes: CAG監査報告書による鉄道駅の飲料水衛生状態に関する指摘であり、実際の感染症患者発生の報告ではない。継続的な曝露リスクはあるが緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: آیا خشکسالی می‌تواند خطر شیوع تب زرد را افزایش دهد؟
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Can drought increase the risk of a yellow fever outbreak?
article.articleSummary: Prolonged droughts may raise yellow fever risk by forcing forest monkeys and Haemagogus mosquitoes to move toward urban areas. A 2015 El Niño–driven drought in central-southern Americas preceded Brazil’s 2016–2019 outbreak, which infected more than 2,000 people and caused about 750 deaths, chiefly in Minas Gerais. The study argues Haemagogus, not Aedes aegypti (which declined after Zika programs), were the key vectors during the outbreak. Computer simulations showed that primate relocation and increased mosquito biting near scarce water best matched the epidemic data. Vaccination and vector control helped curb transmission. The researchers warn that harsher, more frequent droughts—possibly four times per century—could raise future spillover risk. Yellow fever is a viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes, with symptoms from fever and headache to jaundice and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: 干ばつは黄熱病流行のリスクを高める可能性があるか？
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は2016-2019年のブラジルにおける過去の黄熱病流行と干ばつの関連を分析した研究報告であり、現在進行中の新規アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は過去の疫学データに基づく学術的研究の紹介であり、現在の感染症発生イベントではないため、リアルタイムのシグナルとしては該当しない。将来的な気候変動リスクとして経過観察の価値はあるが、緊急のトリアージ対象ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Patient held in isolation in Soroka Hospital tests negative for Ebola after returning from DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola negative in Israel: A patient in isolation at Soroka Medical Center tested negative for Ebola after returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where fever prompted admission. The Health Ministry urged avoiding travel to the DRC and advised anyone returning from the DRC or Uganda to self‑isolate and call the hotline at 5400 if symptoms appear within 21 days. There are currently no confirmed Ebola cases in Israel. The outbreak in the DRC is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola and threatens to be the largest on record, surpassing the 2014–2016 outbreak that totaled 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, per the WHO. In under three months since declaration, over 4,381 cases and 2,011 deaths have been reported; it took about 12 months in 2014 to reach that toll. Ebola is not airborne and spreads via direct contact with symptomatic patients or their blood, body fluids, or secretions. Israel is monitoring and bolstering systemic preparedness.

triage.headline_ja: DRC滞在後にソロカ病院で隔離されていた患者、エボラ検査で陰性
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国(DRC)における進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが、宣言から3か月未満で4,381症例・2,011死亡に達し、2014-2016年の西アフリカ大流行を上回る規模になる恐れがあると報告されており、国際的な渡航制限措置も発生している。
triage.notes: 記事はイスラエルでの陰性症例を報じているが、主題はDRCで進行中の大規模エボラアウトブレイク（Bundibugyo型）。シエラレオネ・リベリア・ウガンダ・ギニアは2014-2016年流行の比較対象として言及されているのみで、現在の発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。イスラエルは対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai News : धक्कादायक! वाढदिवसाच्या केकमध्ये आढळली पाल, 11 जणांना विषबाधा; 4 जण ICUमध्ये
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mumbai News: Shocking! Maggots found in a birthday cake; 11 people poisoned; 4 in the ICU.
article.articleSummary: Eleven people in Nalasopara East's Lakshmi Nagar, Mumbai, fell ill after a birthday party at Nilkanth Apartments when cake was served. Some attendees alleged maggots in the cake amid reports of food poisoning. Four patients are in the ICU and seven in the general ward at Vijay Lakshmi Hospital. Police are investigating, with cake and food samples sent for laboratory testing; the exact cause has not been confirmed. The incident underscores a potential foodborne outbreak linked to cake consumption at a residential party, with authorities awaiting official findings on the contamination source.

triage.headline_ja: ムンバイニュース：衝撃！誕生日ケーキにトカゲ（ウジ虫）が発見され、11人が食中毒、4人がICUに入院

triage.notes: 単発の食中毒事例であり、感染症アウトブレイクとしての特徴は見られない。原因物質・病原体は未特定で、感染症由来かも不明。

article.articleHeadline: الأمم المتحدة: وفاة شخص بـ"إيبولا" كل 30 دقيقة في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UN: One person dies of Ebola every 30 minutes in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is causing a death every 30 minutes, UN humanitarian affairs chief Tom Fletcher said, calling it the fastest-spreading outbreak ever and urging the international community to intensify response and solidarity. He warned far more people are at risk, with several countries pledging about $300 million to an Ebola response fund. Fletcher cautioned that Ebola is “winning” in the DRC but stressed the response must keep pace. He highlighted needs for water, sanitation, and health services in affected areas, and announced 20 additional staff being deployed to the front lines, while calling for more resources: double the teams ensuring safe and dignified burials, triple the treatment capacity, and improve contact tracing and deployment of more experienced managers.

triage.headline_ja: 国連:コンゴ民主共和国でエボラにより30分ごとに1人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 国連高官が「史上最速の拡大」と警告し、致死的なアウトブレイクが継続、国際支援(3億ドル規模)が動員されているためIHR基準・社会的関心ともに高い。
triage.notes: 国連人道問題調整官の発言に基づく報道。具体的な感染者数・地域の詳細は本文に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Health Tips: मानसून में बढ़ा डेंगू का खतरा, बचाव के लिए अपनाएं ये आसान उपाय
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health Tips: Dengue risk increases during the monsoon season; adopt these simple measures to prevent dengue.
article.articleSummary: As of August 16, 2026, dengue risk rises in Khargone district during the monsoon, with two new dengue patients reported in Kunda Nagar and Anand Nagar, triggering an intensified public-health alert. Authorities have accelerated larval surveys, fogging, and removal of breeding sites in affected areas. District Malaria Officer Dr. Manoj Patidar said about 190,000 homes have been surveyed since January, with Aedes larvae found at roughly 7,500 sites and eliminated. Of about 500 suspected cases tested, 19 dengue cases were confirmed. Reported symptoms include high fever, pain behind the eyes, headache, body and joint pain, vomiting, fatigue, and a red rash. The health advisory urges immediate testing for suspected cases and prevention: a weekly dry day, cleaning water containers, preventing stagnation, covering tanks, wearing long sleeves, and using mosquito nets.

article.articleHeadline: Вспышка Эболы в Конго стремительно распространяется: врачи не успевают отслеживать контакты
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo is spreading rapidly; doctors can't keep up with contact tracing.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is spreading rapidly in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with health workers unable to keep up with contact tracing. Between 60% and 70% of new cases are detected among people who were not previously monitored as contacts, meaning infections are often identified only after symptom onset, allowing transmission to others. Since the outbreak began, more than 4,700 cases have been reported and over 2,200 people have died. The outbreak's mortality pace is nearly three times faster to reach 2,200 deaths compared with the 2014-2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic. In response, the United Nations has allocated an additional $30.5 million in emergency aid to fight the outbreak. Source: Associated Press (via unn.ua). Published 2026-08-16.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行が急速に拡大、医師は接触者追跡が追いつかない
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準に複数該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク）し、致死率・症例数ともに大規模かつ急拡大しているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ東部の状況に焦点を当てており、アンゴラについては言及がないため除外。UNによる3050万ドルの緊急支援が既に実施されており、致死ペースが2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行の約3倍という点は特筆すべき異常性。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : le bilan de l'épidémie d'Ebola s'alourdit à 2 272 morts
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The Ebola outbreak death toll rises to 2,272.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,272 Ebola deaths from 4,843 laboratory-confirmed cases across 55 health zones in six provinces (Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo) as of August 14, 2026. Ituri remains the epicenter. There are 777 patients in isolation or hospitalized, and 1,006 recovered since outbreak onset. Case fatality rate stands at 46.9%; contact tracing completion is 83.2%. Authorities continue epidemiological surveillance, investigation of suspected cases, and follow-up of contacts. Public health capacity is strengthened with a new Ebola Treatment Centre in Mongbwalu, while community sensitization and mobilization persist in affected areas. The outbreak was officially declared on May 15; Africa CDC notes transmission could have begun as early as February. Ongoing measures include monitoring in the six provinces and across 55 health zones.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:エボラ出血熱の流行による死者数が2,272人に増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で6州55保健地区にわたる大規模なエボラ流行が継続し、致死率46.9%と極めて高く、公衆衛生上重大な影響がある。
triage.notes: 2026年5月15日に公式宣言されたエボラ流行が継続中で、Africa CDCは2月にはすでに伝播が始まっていた可能性を指摘。国際的な支援（Africa CDC、治療センター新設）が行われている。

article.articleHeadline: La guerra del ébola: conflictos armados, lucha por recursos y epidemias en uno de los países más pobres de mundo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola War: Armed Conflicts, the Struggle for Resources, and Epidemics in One of the World's Poorest Countries
article.articleSummary: The article links Ebola outbreaks to global health preparedness, recounting Spain’s experience and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) crisis. It details nurse Teresa Romero’s Ebola infection in Madrid after caring for two West African priests repatriated from Liberia and Sierra Leone in 2014, her subsequent 30‑day isolation, and public scrutiny of safeguards. It notes that this era exposed gaps in standard isolation facilities, prompting reforms culminating in Spain’s UATAN network (Unidades de Aislamiento y Tratamiento de Alto Nivel) established in 2015, now comprising seven centers and 16 high‑level isolation rooms. Madrid’s Gómez Ulla Hospital hosts the largest unit with seven beds and an integrated laboratory. The unit recently quarantined 14 Spaniards from the MV Hondius for hantavirus. The piece concludes that the current DRC Ebola outbreak could become the worst in its history, underscoring how poverty, conflict, and resource struggles heighten global health risks.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの戦争：武力紛争、資源をめぐる争い、そして世界最貧国のひとつでの感染症流行

triage.notes: 記事はスペインの高度隔離病棟（UATAN）の歴史と2014年の看護師感染事例が主題であり、DRCの現行エボラ流行については「史上最悪になり得る」との言及に留まり、具体的な最新データは含まれていない。スペイン・リベリア・シエラレオネは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Indian Railways Fails Basic Amenities Test, CAG Flags Contamination, Presence Of E. Coli | Outlook India
article.articleSummary: Total coliforms bacteria, including E. coli, were found in drinking water samples from taps at Indian Railways platforms: 49 stations in eight zones (2022-23) and 56 stations in nine zones (2023-24). The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) directed authorities to implement strict water safety measures. Key recommendations mandate compliance with inspection protocols for water supply systems and comprehensive testing of drinking water quality, covering all parameters under the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol. The findings signal potential health risks from rail-water consumption and prompt enhanced monitoring and corrective actions across affected zones and stations. This report emphasizes compliance across eight and nine zones studied, with implications for public health and rail-water safety.

article.articleHeadline: La epidemia de ébola en el Congo provoca una muerte cada 30 minutos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic in Congo causes one death every 30 minutes.
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo—driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus—poses the fastest-growing epidemic on record. The outbreak has claimed more than 2,180 lives and infected over 4,660 people across six provinces, with Ituri province bearing the heaviest burden (more than 3,400 cases). The UN warns the crisis is compounded by armed conflict and severe malnutrition. There is concern about regional spillover after cases were detected in neighboring Uganda and near the border with South Sudan. The disease, for which there is no licensed vaccine or proven specific treatment, prompted emergency measures on 15 May. The UN allocated an additional $30.5 million from the Central Emergency Response Fund and urged tripling treatment capacity, doubling safe burial teams, and strengthening humanitarian and food assistance in isolation centers.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、30分ごとに1人が死亡
