article.articleHeadline: Ebola, oltre 4.600 casi in Congo: l'epidemia accelera e mette a dura prova i soccorsi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, over 4,600 cases in Congo: the epidemic accelerates and puts the relief efforts to the test.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 4,600 confirmed cases and at least 2,100 deaths. The epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, shows the fastest growth yet, with leaders warning it could exceed the West Africa 2014–2016 outbreak; WHO chief Tedros calls it the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record. There are currently no approved vaccines or therapies for Bundibugyo, and the case fatality is reported between 25% and 50%. Response is hampered by conflict, weak health infrastructure, staff and PPE shortages, fear, and misinformation. In Bunia, motorcycle taxi drivers report reduced capacity per ride, harming earnings. Frontline workers report three months of unpaid wages and protest resignations. The UN notes most Ebola deaths occur in communities due to late presentation or lack of access to care. Africa CDC confirms spread to a new province.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ、コンゴで4,600人超の感染例:流行が加速し救援活動を圧迫
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行が4,600例・2,100人超の死者に達し、史上2番目の規模とWHOが言及。ワクチン・治療薬未承認、新州への拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事本文では言及なし。Bundibugyo株による流行で、致死率25-50%、承認済みワクチン・治療薬なし。新州への拡大をAfrica CDCが確認しており、国際的拡大リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: El Congo aumenta a 2,272 la cifra de muertos y 4,843 los casos confirmados de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Congo raises the death toll to 2,272 and the number of confirmed Ebola cases to 4,843.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola outbreak: 2,272 deaths and 4,843 confirmed cases as of 14 August, with a fatality rate of 46.9%. About 777 patients are in isolation or hospitalised, and 1,006 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 83.2%. Transmission spans six provinces—Ituri (epicentre), Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, Bas-Uele (first death confirmed this week), and South Kivu where no new cases have been recorded for ~80 days. WHO notes the virus began circulating in eastern DRC in February, with a Science study suggesting January. This is the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the fastest-growing by cases, second-highest in infections historically, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak (2,299 deaths; 3,481 cases). The circulating Bundibugyo strain has a 30–50% fatality rate and no licensed vaccine or specific treatment. Uganda reported 20 infections (15 imported from the DRC) and two deaths; Uganda declared Ebola-free on 28 July.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、エボラ出血熱の死者数2,272人、確定症例数4,843人に増加
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約47%、6州にまたがる大規模流行で史上最速拡大かつ感染者数で歴代2位の規模。ウガンダへの越境感染も確認されており、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が明らか。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの感染例（20例、うち15例はDRCからの輸入例）も報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン・特異的治療法が未承認である点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: تحذيرات أممية من تسارع تفشي فيروس "إيبولا" في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UN warns of accelerating Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: August 16, 2026: The United Nations and the World Health Organization warn of an accelerating Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The outbreak is described as the largest on record in the DRC and the fastest-spreading to date, expanding from an initial focus in the Mongbabu area of Ituri Province to 54 health zones across six provinces. Latest figures from the DRC’s Ministry of Information show 4,727 confirmed cases and 2,214 deaths, a case fatality rate of about 46.8%. UN humanitarian affairs chief Tom Fletcher says the virus is killing roughly one person every 30 minutes and calls for doubling international relief, surveillance, isolation, and treatment efforts to curb transmission and support affected communities. WHO emphasizes rapid expansion and urges intensified response measures to contain the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: 国連、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラウイルス流行の加速に警鐘
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ型）の史上最大・最速拡大流行であり、致死率約46.8%、6州54保健地域に拡大するなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高いため。
triage.notes: 国連・WHOが国際的な支援拡大を要請しており、フルリスク評価（RRA）への移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola au Nord-Kivu: une ambulance médicalisée remise à l'hôpital général de Musienene pour renforcer la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in North Kivu: a medicalized ambulance handed over to Musienene General Hospital to strengthen the response.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola response asset, a medically equipped ambulance, was officially handed over on August 15, 2026 to the Musienene General Reference Hospital in the Musienene Chiefdom, Lubero Territory, North Kivu. Funded by the central government via the North Kivu military governor, the ambulance aims to strengthen management of suspected or confirmed Ebola virus disease cases and shorten transfer times to specialized facilities. Prisca Luanda Kamala, lead coordinator of the governor’s health response, stated the vehicle will transport Ebola patients under appropriate conditions, used exclusively for Ebola-related activities including patient transport and health logistics, and will not be mixed with other patients. Ugandan medical staff and provincial response coordination accompanied the ceremony, underscoring ongoing and intensified Ebola outbreak response in North Kivu.

triage.headline_ja: 北キブ州のエボラ:リポストを強化するためムシエネネ総合病院に医療用救急車が引き渡される
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR上重大な公衆衛生リスクを有し、国際的拡大の可能性がある既知の継続的アウトブレイクであり、対応強化のための資源投入が続いていることからフルRRA対象とする。
triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラ対応強化（救急車供与）に関する続報であり、新規症例数や感染拡大の具体的データは記載されていない。ウガンダの医療スタッフの関与が言及されているが、発生地はDRC北キブ州に限定される。

article.articleHeadline: After CAG flags E. Coli in drinking water, Railways announces major upgrade at 20,000 locations
article.articleSummary: Eight of 49 railway stations tested positive for E. coli in drinking water, with samples from Mumbai, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Jharkhand stations contaminated. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report notes lapses in inspection frequency and shortfalls in residual chlorine testing, bacteriological and chemical analysis, and that several parameters under the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Protocol were not tested, resulting in unsatisfactory water quality. In response, Indian Railways announced a major upgrade: installation of Tank to Tap water filtration and monitoring systems at around 20,000 locations, replacement of old water tanks, and regular source and outlet water testing. A centralized monitoring system, cleaned storage tanks, and periodic progress reports will improve accountability; Rail Board will oversee implementation. The CAG recommended strict adherence to protocols for water supply inspection and comprehensive testing across all parameters.

triage.headline_ja: CAGが飲料水中の大腸菌汚染を指摘、鉄道は2万か所で大規模改修を発表
triage.triage_reason: 水質管理の行政監査報告に基づく制度改善策の発表であり、疾病の集団発生や公衆衛生上の急性リスクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事は感染症の集団発生ではなく、監査報告(CAG)に基づく鉄道の水質管理インフラ改善策を報じるもの。具体的な患者発生や健康被害の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : une hécatombe silencieuse
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: a silent catastrophe
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reports 4,843 confirmed cases and 2,272 deaths, a case fatality rate of 46.9%. Across six provinces with Ituri as the epicenter, 50 health zones are affected. A new treatment center opened in Mongbwalu, and contact tracing is 83.2% effective. Conflict, mistrust, and remote areas complicate the response, challenging surveillance, care delivery, and patient management. Currently, 777 patients are hospitalized. The outbreak's proximity to Uganda raises concern for cross-border spread, while international attention remains limited. As of 2026-08-16, the crisis remains underrecognized internationally. As of 2026-08-16, the epidemic continues to unfold with high lethality and geographic reach, while the international community's attention remains limited.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：静かな大惨事
triage.triage_reason: 致死率46.9%、感染者4,843人・死者2,272人と大規模かつ深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、ウガンダとの国境付近で越境拡大のリスクも指摘されているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境拡大懸念が記載されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。国際的な注目度が低いことが記事内で強調されており、支援ニーズが高い可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : les autorités sanitaires alertent sur l'évasion de 19 malades des centres de traitement au Nord-Kivu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Health authorities warn of the escape of 19 patients from treatment centers in North Kivu.
article.articleSummary: 19 Ebola patients escaped from treatment centers in four health zones of North Kivu's Grand Nord-Kivu: Katwa (7), Butembo (3), Beni (1), and Musienene (8). As of August 14 (update published August 15), 591 confirmed cases have been recorded with 404 deaths and 70 recoveries (case fatality rate 68%), with the outbreak touching 12 of the province’s 34 health zones. Escapes raise renewed transmission risk as patients return to communities; persistent community resistance drives ongoing awareness efforts. In response, Ugandan doctors arrived in Butembo to bolster teams in Butembo and Beni, after Uganda declared its outbreak over in July following 42 days without deaths. UNICEF delivered six vehicles (two per Katwa, Butembo, Beni) to strengthen prevention and infection control, and Musienene received a staffed ambulance to transport suspected/confirmed cases to specialized facilities.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱:保健当局、北キブ州の治療センターから患者19人が逃走したことを警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の進行中のアウトブレイク（591症例、致死率68%）に加え、治療センターからの患者逃走という異常事態が地域社会への感染再拡大リスクを高めており、国際支援（ウガンダ、UNICEF）も既に動員されている。
triage.notes: ウガンダは自国のアウトブレイク終息後に医療従事者を派遣する支援国として登場しているため、発生国としては含めない。致死率68%と高く、患者の地域社会への逃走は感染拡大・対策妨害のリスクを著しく高める重大な事象。

article.articleHeadline: Telangana Records 230 Dengue Cases In 4 Months
article.articleSummary: 230 dengue cases were recorded in Telangana between April and July, with no dengue deaths reported, according to NCVBDC data. The figure is provisional and not August’s cumulative; the national database last updated July 25, and gaps arise from differing reporting periods, with state systems capturing recent district activity. In the week ending Aug 6, GHMC accounted for 532 cases, followed by Rangareddy (196), Warangal Urban (142), Medchal-Malkajgiri (136), Karimnagar (93), Nizamabad (89), Khammam (85), Bhadradri Kothagudem (82). Across Telangana, counts: 2021 7,135; 2022 8,972; 2023 8,016; 2024 10,077; 2025 8,412, with 2023 recording one dengue death and no deaths in 2021-2022, 2024-2025. For Hyderabad (GHMC), 266 cases Jan–July 13, 2026, with 127 lab-confirmed, down from 2025 (570) and 2024 (821). Pediatrician notes influenza is prevalent; dengue cases are sporadic. Precautions: protect against mosquitoes, avoid standing water; switch off liquid vapourisers before sleeping due to allergy risk.

triage.headline_ja: テランガーナ州、4か月で230件のデング熱症例を記録
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・季節性インフルエンザともに例年並みの発生状況で死亡例もほぼなく、公衆衛生上の異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 例年の季節性デング熱・インフルエンザ報告記事であり、症例数は過去数年と比較して低〜同水準。死亡例もほぼ報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: La tuberculose multi résistante reste une crise sanitaire en RDC (Programme national de lutte contre la tuberculose) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis remains a health crisis in the DRC (National Tuberculosis Control Programme) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). In Kinshasa, at the close of a two-day journalists’ capacity-building workshop, Dr. Fina Mawete of the National Tuberculosis Control Programme warned that only 300 diagnostic machines serve 2,000 health facilities, hindering early detection of MDR-TB. She urged at least one diagnostic machine per facility to accelerate detection and advance the 2035 elimination target. Dr. Romain Kibadi noted government TB funding at only 3%, with 97% of resources coming from external financing, a level deemed insufficient. He called for a larger health budget to sustain the response. A durable partnership between the National TB Programme and journalists was signed to promote accurate, stigma-free reporting, with a network to monitor field actions and amplify prevention, screening, and treatment messages nationwide across all provinces.

triage.headline_ja: 多剤耐性結核はDRCにおいて依然として健康危機である（結核対策国家プログラム）- ACP
triage.triage_reason: 既知の慢性的な公衆衛生課題（MDR-TB対策の資金・診断機器不足）に関する報道であり、新規または異常な発生ではないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 本記事は既存の結核対策プログラムに関する啓発・資金不足の課題報告であり、急性の感染症アウトブレイクを示すものではない。継続的な資金・医療体制の課題として認識されるが、緊急トリアージ対象ではない。

article.articleHeadline: E. coli bacteria found in water at railway stations, says CAG report
article.articleSummary: India's Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) found E. coli bacteria in drinking-water samples from taps at platform water stations across multiple railway zones (49 stations in eight zones during 2022-23; 56 stations in nine zones during 2023-24). Total coliforms including E. coli detected; bacteriological tests beyond total coliforms unsatisfactory at eight stations in four zones (2022-23) and 11 stations in five zones (FY24). Samples from Mumbai, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand. Inspection of water supply systems not carried out as prescribed; shortfalls in testing residual chlorine, bacteriological and chemical analyses. Health risk: some E. coli strains cause diarrhoea; higher risk for children and older adults. Government response: Railways launching Tank to Tap filtration at 20,000 locations; replacement of water tanks; centralized monitoring; periodic water-quality reports; aim to address CAG observations.

triage.headline_ja: 鉄道駅の水からE.コリ菌検出、CAG報告書が指摘
triage.triage_reason: 実際の感染者・発症例の報告はなく、会計監査院（CAG）による水質検査結果の指摘に留まるインフラ・行政報告であり、感染症アウトブレイクのシグナルとは言えない。
triage.notes: 本記事は実際の感染者発生報告ではなく、CAGによる鉄道駅の水質監査報告。政府は既にTank to Tapろ過設備導入など対策を実施中であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: E. coli in railway water: Indian Railways to roll out 'tank to tap' plan for safe drinking water across network- Moneycontrol.com
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, E. coli was detected in drinking water at railway water coolers across multiple stations, prompting Indian Railways to launch a 'tank to tap' filtration rollout at about 20,000 locations, replace water tanks, and institute centralized monitoring with regular source- and outlet-testing and periodic reporting. Positive water-cooler tests were reported at Coimbatore and Palakkad Junctions (Southern Railway); Hyderabad (South Central Railway); and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala (Central Railway); Madhupur (Eastern Railway). The CAG’s audit of 512 non-suburban stations (2019-20 to 2023-24) found total coliforms in taps at 49 stations (2022-23) and 56 stations (2023-24) across eight and nine zones, with several bacteriological tests unsatisfactory; 458 stations were deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities (MEA). Some E. coli strains can cause diarrhoea and kidney failure. The action aims to address CAG observations and improve passenger safety and sanitation across the network.

triage.headline_ja: 鉄道飲料水からE.coli検出：インド鉄道、全国で安全飲料水確保のため『タンクからタップまで』計画を展開
triage.triage_reason: 複数駅の飲料水からE.coliが検出され構造的な水質管理問題が指摘されているが、実際の患者発生・症例報告はなく、インド鉄道が既に是正措置を開始しているためフルRRAには進まない。
triage.notes: 記事は水質検査結果とインド鉄道の是正措置（フィルタリング設備導入、監視体制強化）に関するもので、実際の感染症患者発生の報告は含まれていない。CAG監査による既知の構造的問題への対応という位置づけ。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak explodes to 4,665 cases, 2,184 deaths
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths as of August 12, 2026, with an exceptionally high crude case fatality ratio of 46.8%. The outbreak, described by WHO as the largest BVD event in the DRC, has spread to 54 health zones across six provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo and Bas-Uélé—and is expanding faster than previous Ebola outbreaks. Epidemiological week 32 (Aug 3–9) reported 579 cases and 304 deaths, the highest weekly totals to date. Bas-Uélé reported the first infection in Buta, with travel history to Haut-Uélé; symptoms began Aug 4. Ongoing transmission across connected geographic clusters challenges containment amid insecurity, displacement and cross-border movement. France and Uganda have reported imported cases with no secondary transmission; Uganda’s monitoring ends Aug 27 if no new cases. WHO urges rapid scale-up and strengthened surveillance and community engagement.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ(ブンディブギョウイルス病)アウトブレイク、感染4,665例・死亡2,184人に急拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のブンディブギョウイルス病(エボラ関連)アウトブレイクが6州54保健地区に拡大し、致死率46.8%と極めて高く、フランス・ウガンダへの越境例も報告されているため、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: フランス・ウガンダは輸入症例のみで二次感染なしのため、対象国リストにも含まれずverified_locationsから除外。WHOはDRC史上最大のBVDアウトブレイクと表現しており、既にWHO通知・国際対応が進行中の可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de ébola en RDC deja 2.214 muertos y se propaga a nueva zona sanitaria - Tercera Información
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Epidemic in the DRC Leaves 2,214 Dead and Spreads to a New Health Zone - Tercera Información
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has expanded to a seventh health zone in Tshopo, affecting 55 zones across Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. Deaths total 2,214; confirmed cases reach 4,727; 749 patients are in isolation or hospitalized; 976 recovered. Case fatality stands at 46.8% with 82.6% contact tracing. Transmission began in February; the outbreak was declared on 15 May. The Bundibugyo strain has 30–50% fatality and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment. It is the largest and fastest-growing outbreak in DRC history, surpassing 2018–2020 (2,299 deaths, 3,481 cases). The virus spilled into Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths) before Uganda was declared Ebola-free on 28 July. WHO and CDC analyses note potential to reach West Africa 2014–2016 levels. CERF allocated an extra $30.5 million, with $24 million previously; Congo mobilized $50 million.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ流行、死者2,214人に拡大し新たな保健地区へ拡散
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が史上最大規模に拡大し、致死率46.8%、複数州にまたがる拡散とウガンダへの越境感染も発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染は既に収束（7/28にエボラフリー宣言）済みだが、国際的拡大リスクの根拠として言及。ウガンダ・アンゴラは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。CERFやWHO/CDCによる国際支援が既に動いており、西アフリカ2014-2016規模に達する可能性が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: コンゴ民主共和国　"過去最速ペースの流行"エボラ出血熱の死者が2000人超える...感染拡大を抑えるため現地で活動する日本人は（2026年8月17日掲載）｜日テレNEWS NNN
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola outbreak at the fastest pace in history; death toll surpasses 2,000... Japanese on the ground working to curb the spread (Posted August 17, 2026) — Nippon TV News NNN.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is unfolding at the fastest pace in history, with 4,843 confirmed infections and 2,272 deaths since May, centered in the eastern Ituri province. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain for which there are currently no approved vaccines or therapies. Despite a grim outlook, response focuses on prevention and community engagement to curb transmission. Japanese MSF health promoter Aya Sonoda, on the ground in Ituri for about six weeks, reports a continuous flow of patients and daily fatalities. Early misunderstanding and occasional riots complicated initial containment efforts. Burial practices are a notable infection risk; Sonoda emphasizes dissuading high-risk traditional burials and promoting safe handling of the deceased. Containment thus relies on prevention, education, and sustained dialogue with communities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国 "過去最速ペースの流行" エボラ出血熱の死者が2000人超える...感染拡大を抑えるため現地で活動する日本人は（2026年8月17日掲載）
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速ペースのエボラ流行で死者2,000人超、承認済みワクチン・治療薬のない稀な株（ブンディブギョ株）による大規模アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチン・治療薬のないブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス株による流行で、致死率が高く（2,272/4,843）、埋葬慣習を通じた感染拡大リスクが指摘されている。国際的拡大や渡航制限の有無については記事に明記なし。

article.articleHeadline: Nu testas nytt ebolavaccin på människor i Storbritannien | Sveriges Radio
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A New Ebola Vaccine Is Being Tested on Humans in Great Britain | Sveriges Radio
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, researchers in the United Kingdom are one step closer to an effective Ebola vaccine against the variant currently spreading in Kongo-Kinshasa. Four Ebola vaccines are under development, but only one has been tested in humans. A 37-year-old man, Ed Hunt, received the first dose of an Ebola vaccine developed in record time at the University of Oxford. The development effort highlights rapid vaccine design in response to Ebola threats and the progression of human trials, with the Oxford vaccine representing the only candidate yet assessed in people at this stage. No efficacy results are provided in the article.

triage.headline_ja: 英国で新エボラワクチンの人体試験開始
triage.triage_reason: 英国でのワクチン開発・臨床試験に関する報道であり、コンゴ民主共和国での流行株を対象としているが、DRCでの流行状況自体に関する新規情報はなく、直接的な公衆衛生イベントではないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は英国オックスフォード大学でのエボラワクチンの人体試験開始であり、DRCでの流行そのものについての新規情報は含まれていない。DRCは対象ワクチンの対象株の流行地として言及されているのみ。

article.articleHeadline: O que é esporotricose? Surto da doença em gatos exige atenção em Londrina
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is sporotrichosis? Outbreak of the disease in cats calls for attention in Londrina.
article.articleSummary: Sporotrichosis outbreak in Londrina, Paraná, Brazil, driven by Sporothrix brasiliensis. The zoonotic fungal infection, traditionally linked to garden exposure, now shows urban cat-to-human transmission. In 2026, 30 laboratory-confirmed cases were reported in the first seven months, more than double the 14 cases recorded in all of 2025. Feline disease features deep non-healing wounds on the face, snout, ears, and paws, with possible respiratory distress; humans develop nodules at exposure sites after scratches or bites. Early diagnosis is essential to break transmission, with SESA warning of probable underreporting. Municipal actions include isolating affected animals, mandatory reporting, and home investigations, plus sanitary barriers and treatment monitoring for suspected pets. Preventive measures: keep cats indoors, wash wounds promptly, wear rubber gloves when handling injured animals, and disinfect spaces with bleach; never bury carcasses—contact the city for proper cremation or incineration.

triage.headline_ja: スポロトリコーシスとは？ロンドリーナで猫の間で発生した感染症流行に注意喚起
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・パラナ州ロンドリーナで人獣共通感染症（スポロトリコーシス）の症例が増加しているが、局地的でIHR基準の該当は限定的。今後の拡大動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 症例数は2025年通年14件から2026年上半期で30件と倍増しており、都市部での猫からヒトへの伝播が確認されている点が特徴的。ただし発生は特定都市（ロンドリーナ）に限定され、国際的拡大の兆候はない。地方衛生当局（SESA）が過小報告の可能性を指摘しており、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: E. coli found in station drinking water; Railways orders filtration systems at 20,000 locations
article.articleSummary: E. coli detected in drinking water at Indian Railways stations prompted a major upgrade: a 'tank to tap' filtration system at about 20,000 locations, including water coolers. The Comptroller and Auditor General flagged water-quality issues, noting E. coli in taps at 49 stations across eight zones (2022-23) and 56 stations across nine zones (2023-24), with examples Coimbatore, Palakkad, Hyderabad, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala, and Madhupur. E. coli signals possible fecal contamination from sewage or animal/human sources. Testing gaps included insufficient periodic inspections and analyses. Authorities will conduct source-and-outlet testing, monitor water quality at the board level, clean storage tanks, and publish regular reports. The CAG also found 89% of 512 stations deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities and numerous sanitation deficiencies, with many passenger-amenity works delayed, driving rising grievances.

triage.headline_ja: 駅の飲料水から大腸菌検出、鉄道当局が2万カ所にろ過システムを導入へ
triage.triage_reason: 会計監査院の報告に基づく水質管理上の問題であり、急性の集団感染や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す記事ではないため、シグナルとしての優先度は低い。
triage.notes: 本記事は2022-24年の会計監査（CAG）に基づく報告であり、現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイクを報じるものではない。水質管理体制の構造的問題を指摘する行政・インフラ記事に近い。

article.articleHeadline: Expert team carries out containment drive as foot-and-mount disease outbreak hit Arunachal
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak in Arunachal Pradesh's Dibang Valley has killed more than 200 mithuns as of Aug 8, triggering a multi‑agency containment drive. A rapid response team reached Anini on Aug 8, with three specialised teams deployed. On Aug 11, field assessments, epidemiological surveys and sample collection began to map spread and transmission links. A high‑level central team led by VK Teotia arrived on Aug 13 and visited remote areas including Acheso, Angrim Valley, Aropo, Mipi circle, Maro, 9 Kilo and Matu Camp, treating infected animals, distributing medicines and collecting diagnostic samples from mithuns, pigs and goats, with post‑mortems conducted. Goat blood samples were collected at an ITBP camp in Acheso, and biosecurity briefings provided. Inspections occurred at the district veterinary office and cattle breeding farm in Anini. Specimens have been sent to laboratories; vaccination drives will continue biannually, and farmers are urged to report symptoms promptly.

triage.headline_ja: 専門チームがアルナーチャル・プラデーシュ州の口蹄疫アウトブレイクに対する封じ込め活動を実施
triage.triage_reason: 動物（ミトゥン、豚、ヤギ）の口蹄疫アウトブレイクであり、ヒトへの感染や公衆衛生上の影響は報告されていない。動物衛生上の対応事案。
triage.notes: 口蹄疫は動物疾患であり、ヒト感染例の報告はない。インド当局（中央・州レベル）による家畜への封じ込め・ワクチン接種対応が実施中。人獣共通感染症としての公衆衛生リスクは記事内で言及されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Varanasi news: डेंगू से बचाव : डर नहीं, सही जानकारी जरूरी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Varanasi news: Dengue prevention: Don’t be afraid, accurate information is essential.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever concerns in Varanasi during the rainy season, but no dengue cases have been reported yet. Authorities urge accurate information and timely treatment rather than home remedies or social-media guidance. Dengue symptoms can resemble other viral and mosquito-borne illnesses in the early days; red flags include high fever, headache, behind-the-eye pain, muscle and joint pains, nausea, vomiting, and rash. Dr. Indranil Basu, senior physician at 7 Med Hospital, notes that early dengue cannot be confirmed by symptoms alone. In the first week, NS1 antigen or viral RNA testing detects infection, with IgM testing advised about one week after onset. Platelet counts often alarm patients, but platelets can fall and later rise; platelet transfusions should be based on medical need. Do not self-medicate with painkillers; seek doctor guidance promptly to prevent complications during the rainy season.

triage.headline_ja: ヴァラナシニュース: デング熱予防：恐れではなく正確な情報が必要
triage.triage_reason: 現時点でデング熱の症例報告はなく、雨季における一般的な予防啓発記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は症例報告ではなく、季節性のデング熱予防に関する啓発・情報提供記事。現時点で確認された症例なし。

article.articleHeadline: Juazeiro do Norte realiza campanha de vacinação para prevenir o sarampo em crianças e adolescentes - Portal M1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Juazeiro do Norte conducts vaccination campaign to prevent measles among children and adolescents - Portal M1
article.articleSummary: Juazeiro do Norte, Brazil, launches a multivaccination campaign to update vaccination records for people up to age 19 to prevent measles, a highly contagious disease that has historically been a leading cause of child mortality. Doses are also available for individuals up to 59 years old. Eligible residents must visit a Basic Health Unit with their vaccination card, CPF, and SUS card. On August 22, a Day D vaccination across all UBS will be held, with urban posts open 8:00–16:00 and rural posts 8:00–12:00. The Center for Dermatology and Infectious Diseases will participate. The Municipal Health Secretariat states vaccination is the most effective measure against measles, strengthening herd immunity and reducing virus circulation.

triage.headline_ja: ジュアゼイロ・ド・ノルテ、子供・青少年の麻疹予防のためワクチン接種キャンペーンを実施 - ポータルM1
triage.triage_reason: 記事は麻疹の予防的ワクチン接種キャンペーンの案内であり、実際の症例発生や流行を示す情報がないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事は自治体による通常の予防接種キャンペーンの告知であり、麻疹の実際の発生・流行報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Bastar cuts malaria cases by 83% in a decade, shifts focus to prevention
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Bastar has fallen about 83% over the last decade as the government shifts from case detection to prevention in remote tribal villages. The campaign emphasizes sleeping under mosquito nets, prompt testing for fever, and immediate treatment, integrating messages in local languages and through trusted community networks. Traditional figures Baiga, Gunia, and Sirha are engaged in malaria-awareness conferences to tailor prevention and treatment to local customs. Residents are urged not to ignore fever and to contact health workers for testing rather than relying on home remedies. Field workers and Mitanins regularly visit households to ensure nets are used and to facilitate early access to testing and treatment. Enhanced surveillance and testing accompany prevention, early detection, and timely therapy, reflecting closer-to-community services. The aim is to consolidate behavioural changes and prevent a resurgence of malaria.

triage.headline_ja: バスタール地区、マラリア症例を10年間で83%削減、予防重視へ転換
triage.triage_reason: マラリア症例は10年間で83%減少という改善傾向を伝える内容で、公衆衛生上の異常事態や緊急性は見られず、社会的関心も高くない。
triage.notes: 本記事はマラリア対策の成功事例と予防強化策を報じるものであり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Unicef alerta sobre la propagación del cólera en seis países de África occidental y central
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UNICEF warns of the spread of cholera in six countries in West and Central Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of 16 August 2026, UNICEF warns cholera is spreading across six West and Central African countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, Chad, Cameroon, and the Central African Republic. Outbreaks are worsened by seasonal rains, flooding, and displacement from conflicts, with funding shortfalls weakening the response. While specific case counts are not provided, the number of cases is rising. Transmission is moving through shared rivers, trade routes, and population movements, putting millions of children at risk. UNICEF Regional Director Gilles Fagninou stresses the cross-border nature of the outbreak and calls for urgent funding and regional solidarity to secure safe water and a rapid control effort.

triage.headline_ja: ユニセフ、西・中央アフリカ6カ国でのコレラ拡大を警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で「深刻な公衆衛生影響」「国際的拡大」の2つに該当し、対象国であるコンゴ民主共和国を含む複数国での越境コレラ流行が報告されているため、フルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事は西・中央アフリカ6カ国（DRC、コンゴ共和国、ナイジェリア、チャド、カメルーン、中央アフリカ共和国）でのコレラ拡大を報じているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。具体的な症例数・死亡者数は記載されておらず、資金不足と越境的な感染拡大が強調されている。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Avian Influenza A H5N1

article.articleHeadline: Is bird flu infecting humans? How would we know?
article.articleSummary: Bird flu (avian influenza) H5N1, 2.3.4.4b, is circulating among birds on the Australian mainland. Since June, Australia has reported at least one mass mortality event in birds; no human cases from the current strain have occurred in Australia as of 16 August 2026. Globally, since 2003 WHO has recorded about 1,000 human H5N1 cases with 479 deaths; seven human cases have been reported in Cambodia, Bangladesh and India with two deaths. 2.3.4.4b generally causes mild disease in humans, though a few severe cases have occurred in the US; no Australian humans have been infected by 2.3.4.4b. A related 2.3.2.1a case occurred in a child who returned from overseas travel. Risk to humans remains low; transmission is via close contact with infected birds, not sustained human-to-human spread. Testing relies on clinician suspicion for a bird flu–specific test; oseltamivir may be offered. Report sick or dead birds to 1800 675 888.

triage.headline_ja: 鳥インフルエンザはヒトに感染しているのか？どうすればわかるのか？
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はオーストラリアにおける鳥類間でのH5N1流行状況とグローバルな過去症例数を解説する教育的記事であり、新規の異常事態や急性の公衆衛生上の脅威を報告するものではない。ヒトへのリスクは低いと明記されている。
triage.notes: 記事はオーストラリアの鳥インフルエンザ状況の解説記事。India、Bangladesh、Cambodiaは2003年以降の累計症例数（過去の歴史的統計）として言及されているのみで、現在進行中の発生国ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。オーストラリア自体は対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Nia-Nia: l'hygiène aux frontières propose un plan d'action sécurisant la riposte - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Nia-Nia: border hygiene proposes an action plan to safeguard the response - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola response in Nia-Nia, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo, focuses on border hygiene-driven action planning to safeguard operations at PK51 in the Nia-Nia health zone. The plan centers on three axes: permanent security of sites and response teams; securing key border checkpoints bordering neighboring provinces; and strengthening collaboration among health services, security services, local authorities, and communities, per Dr. Théophile Ponde, provincial coordinator of the National Border Hygiene Program (PNHF/Ituri). It also calls for identifying strategic checkpoints needing permanent security presence and 24/7 service delivery, establishing a rapid alert mechanism for incidents, and continuous monitoring of the situation. The objective is to anticipate incidents, protect response teams, and ensure the continuity of Ebola outbreak response activities in the PK51 mining area.

triage.headline_ja: ニアニアのエボラ出血熱:国境衛生局が対応活動を保全する行動計画を提案 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク対応に関する記事であり、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク・渡航貿易制限リスク）を複数満たすため。
triage.notes: 既存のエボラアウトブレイク対応の一環として、国境地帯（鉱山地区PK51）における治安確保と関係機関連携強化に関する行動計画の記事。既知の流行状況下での運用強化情報であり、フルリスク評価による最新状況の確認が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : la négligence des mesures barrières constaté auprès des déplacés de l'Ituri - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Negligence in barrier measures observed among the displaced people of Ituri - ACP
article.articleSummary: Displaced people in Bunia, Ituri province, northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, are showing negligence of Ebola barrier measures. Handwashing practices have declined; corpse handling has resumed at relocation sites, with people touching and kissing bodies, increasing transmission risk. Some displaced believe the outbreak is over, leading to lax hygiene and removal of handwashing stations. Olivier Karba, spokesperson for the Association of the Displaced and War Victims of Ituri (ADVG), warns the disease persists and could be worsening. He emphasizes strict adherence to corpse handling rules and barrier measures, and calls for site managers and displaced people to strengthen vigilance. The message underlines that Ebola still exists and requires renewed emphasis on hygiene and proper handling of corpses by authorized personnel to prevent transmission.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:イトゥリ州の避難民の間で感染予防対策の軽視が確認される - ACP
triage.triage_reason: エボラは重篤な感染症であり、活動性のアウトブレイク地域で避難民の間に予防対策の軽視（手洗い停止、遺体への接触・接吻の再開）が確認されており、感染再燃・拡大のリスクが高いためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は新規症例の確認ではなく、既存のエボラ流行地における避難民の予防行動の低下（手洗い停止、遺体への接触等）を報告している。現地NGO（ADVG）が警戒強化を呼びかけており、感染再拡大の前兆となり得るためモニタリングとRRAでの詳細確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uele : des difficultés signalées au centre de traitement Ebola à Isiro - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Haut-Uele: difficulties reported at the Ebola treatment center in Isiro - ACP
article.articleSummary: Isiro, Haut-Uele, northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, reports difficulties at the Ebola Treatment Center (CTE) that hinder normal operation. Dr. David Kamalu, chief medical officer of Isiro's General Reference Hospital, said upgrading works continue but intermittent delays persist, including securing the ceded building, consolidating access through a single entrance, and extending electrification, water, and hygienic facilities. Nevertheless, the center is functional and has recorded its first cured patients. Supplies and equipment are reportedly adequate for care providers; if needs arise, requests are escalated to the hierarchy and replenishment proceeds automatically. Nine patients are under treatment at Isiro's CTE: eight have tested positive for Ebola; one is awaiting results. The remarks come after the governor's visit during the ceremony releasing the first cured patients.

triage.headline_ja: オー・ウエレ州：イジロのエボラ治療センターで困難が報告される - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認されたエボラ患者（陽性8名）が治療センターで治療中であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラアウトブレイク（イジロ、オー・ウエレ州）における治療センターの運営上の課題（電力・水・衛生設備の未整備等）に関する続報。陽性8名・判定待ち1名が治療中で、初の治癒退院者が出たとの報告あり。既知のアウトブレイクの進展として引き続き監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Com 18 mortes confirmadas por febre maculosa em SP, especialista da UMC alerta para diagnóstico precoce e prevenção
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: With 18 confirmed deaths from Brazilian spotted fever in São Paulo, a specialist from UMC warns about early diagnosis and prevention.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian spotted fever has caused 18 deaths and 19 confirmed cases in the state of São Paulo through July 2026, with fatalities concentrated in Piracicaba, Americana, Sorocaba, Campinas, São José dos Campos, Santo André, and São Bernardo do Campo; Alto Tietê reports no cases this year, though risk remains in rural, trail, and woodland areas. Early diagnosis is crucial to prevent severe illness. Transmitted by ticks infected with Rickettsia rickettsii, the disease can be carried indoors by dogs. Initial symptoms are nonspecific, with fever, body pains, headache and malaise; by day three a red rash and purplish lesions on hands and feet may develop, signaling vascular involvement. Mortality can reach 80% if antibiotics are delayed. Laboratory confirmation may take up to two weeks, so treatment should start promptly when fever follows forest exposure. Prevention includes long pants, boots, light-colored clothing, prompt body and clothing checks, avoiding tall grass, and tick prevention for dogs.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロ州でブラジル紅斑熱による死亡18例確認、UMCの専門家が早期診断と予防を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: マダニ媒介性で人-人感染なく国際的拡大リスクは低いが、致死率が高く(未治療で最大80%)、州内で継続的な曝露リスクがあるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本疾患はダニ媒介性（Rickettsia rickettsii）で人-人感染はなく、ブラジルの地方風土病として例年発生している。国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威というよりは地域の季節性公衆衛生課題と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19: China registró más de 500.000 casos en un mes y crece la preocupación
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19: China registered more than 500,000 cases in a month and concern grows.
article.articleSummary: China registered 522,000 COVID-19 cases in July, rising from 79,000 in June and earlier monthly tallies of 23,477 in April and 21,861 in May, indicating a rapid surge in infections. Despite the surge, deaths remained comparatively low relative to earlier pandemic peaks. COVID-19 is classified in China as a Category B infectious disease, with authorities expecting one or two periods of higher circulation per year. Surveillance continues to track not only case counts but also severe cases, hospitalizations, and circulating variants. NB.1.8.1 was the predominant lineage, and health authorities reported no new variants implying additional public-health risk. The World Health Organization maintains global monitoring of cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and variant circulation, noting that testing and notification systems have evolved since the early pandemic. The July surge places COVID-19 again under international scrutiny to assess impacts on severe outcomes in the coming weeks.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19:中国で1か月に50万人以上の感染例、懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: 中国でのCOVID-19症例数急増が報告されているが、死亡率は低く新規変異株も確認されていないため、季節的な流行拡大の範囲内とみられる。ただし規模の大きさから経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: COVID-19は中国でCategory B感染症に分類され、年1〜2回の流行期が想定されている。今回の症例急増は季節性の範囲内とみられ、重症例・死亡増加の明確な兆候はないが、今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: エボラ熱「患者減らない」　派遣の日本人職員逼迫訴え
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: "The number of patients isn't decreasing" — dispatched Japanese staff say they are being stretched to the limit.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo persists, with MSF staff Aya Sonoda, 50, reporting near-capacity treatment facilities in Ituri province’s Bunia city and a patient load that shows little decline. Since early July, she has spent about six weeks mainly handling the transfer of deceased patients. The WHO emergency declaration for the outbreak is now three months old with no clear end in sight. According to the DR Congo health ministry, the country has recorded more than 4,800 Ebola infections and over 2,200 deaths. The report underscores ongoing strain on frontline workers and facilities amid this protracted outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱「患者減らない」　派遣の日本人職員逼迫訴え
triage.triage_reason: WHOが緊急事態を宣言してから3か月が経過し、感染者4,800人超・死者2,200人超と深刻な公衆衛生への影響が継続しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 既にWHOが緊急事態宣言を出している大規模かつ長期化するエボラ流行であり、現地医療体制の逼迫が続いている。国際的拡大リスクや渡航制限に関する直接的言及は記事内になく不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: 【茨城新聞】エボラ熱「患者減らない」
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Ibaraki Shimbun] Ebola fever: 'The number of patients is not decreasing.'
article.articleSummary: Despite the WHO emergency declaration three months ago, the Ebola virus disease outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo shows no sign of abating. MSF staff member Aya Sonoda, dispatched to Ituri Province’s Bunia, reported treatment facilities nearly always at capacity as patient numbers persist. She spent roughly early July to mid-August at an MSF site, mainly involved in handing over the deceased. Congo’s health ministry tallies more than 4,800 infections and over 2,200 deaths. The ongoing transmission and strained medical response underscore the lack of a clear end in sight while international agencies monitor the situation.

triage.headline_ja: 【茨城新聞】エボラ熱「患者減らない」
triage.triage_reason: WHO緊急事態宣言から3か月経過してもコンゴ民主共和国東部でエボラ出血熱の感染が収束せず、死者2200人超・感染者4800人超と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響が続いており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: WHOによる緊急事態宣言後も感染拡大が継続しており、MSFなど国際機関の医療支援体制が逼迫している状況。国際的拡大や渡航制限への影響については記事内に明示的な記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: エボラ熱「患者減らない」 派遣の日本人職員逼迫訴え｜全国のニュース｜Web東奥
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola fever: "Patients aren't decreasing" Dispatched Japanese staff say they are being overwhelmed | National News | Web Tohoku
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease remains uncontrolled in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with MSF staff reporting overwhelmed treatment facilities and no decline in cases. Aya Sonoda, a 50-year-old Médecins Sans Frontières worker dispatched to Bunia in Ituri Province, described in an online interview on August 13 that facilities are almost always at capacity and patient numbers are not decreasing. The World Health Organization had declared a public health emergency three months earlier, and there is little prospect of a rapid end to transmission. In the DRC, the Ministry of Health reports more than 4,800 Ebola infections and over 2,200 deaths. Sonoda spent about six weeks starting in early July at an MSF facility mainly involved in handing over corpses. The piece underscores the ongoing strain amid a continuing outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱「患者減らない」 派遣の日本人職員逼迫訴え｜全国のニュース｜Web東奥
triage.triage_reason: WHOが緊急事態を宣言済みで、致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国東部で制御不能な状態にあり、感染者数・死亡者数も多く公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が認められるためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: WHOは既に公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言済み。4,800人以上の感染者、2,200人以上の死者が報告されており、アウトブレイクは継続中で終息の見通しが立っていない。

article.articleHeadline: Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in country's history
article.articleSummary: Aug 16, 2026: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 2,325 people, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history and surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic. The DRC public health institute’s latest report lists 4,945 confirmed cases, including 101 new cases detected in the previous 24 hours. The article provides no details on symptoms, transmission chains, laboratory confirmation methods, infection source, or imported/exported cases. This reflects an ongoing outbreak within the country, with no further locations or geographic breakdown provided in the report.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、同国史上最悪の規模に
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱で2,325人死亡、4,945症例確認と同国史上最悪の流行規模であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 症状、感染経路、検査方法、感染源、越境事例についての詳細情報は記事に記載なし。続報でのRRA実施が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo now deadliest in country's history
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the deadliest in the country’s history, with 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak’s 2,299 deaths. The United Nations warned that Ebola is winning in the DRC, and the epidemic is now killing about one person every 30 minutes. This remains an ongoing outbreak as of 16 August 2026. The report provides no details on the infection source, laboratory confirmation, or imported/exported cases. The article is breaking news and being updated, with more details to be published shortly.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、同国史上最悪の事態に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪規模のエボラ流行が継続中であり、致死率も高く、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威として深刻な影響が認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断した。
triage.notes: 国連が「エボラが勝っている」と警告し、30分に1人が死亡するペースと報道。感染源や検査確定情報、越境事例については記事に記載なし。続報での詳細確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 剛果伊波拉疫情奪2325命　創該國史上最致命紀錄 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Congo Ebola outbreak has claimed 2,325 lives, making it the deadliest outbreak in the country's history.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo is grappling with an Ebola outbreak that has claimed 2,325 lives, the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history and surpassing the 2018–2020 surge. The latest government data, reported by Reuters, show cumulative confirmed Ebola cases reaching 4,945, with 101 new confirmed cases detected in the past 24 hours, signaling that transmission remains intense as of August 17, 2026. The figures illustrate a sustained and severe outbreak in the DRC, underscoring the ongoing public health challenge posed by Ebola in the country. The report compiles official figures from the DRC government and Reuters, highlighting the critical trend of rising case counts alongside a rising death toll in this outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: E coli found in drinking water, rail stations lack basic facilities: CAG
article.articleSummary: E. coli contamination was detected in drinking water at eight railway stations: Coimbatore and Palakkad junctions (Southern Railway), Hyderabad (South Central Railway), CSMT, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan and Lonavala (Central Railway), and Madhupur (Eastern Railway). CAG also found bacteriological analysis of drinking water not carried out at 59 stations in six zones, and coliforms detected in taps at 49 stations in eight zones (2022-23) and 56 stations in nine zones (2023-24). Overall, 458 of 512 selected stations were deficient in minimum essential amenities such as seating, sanitary facilities, dustbins and electronic train indicator boards, with CSMT, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi and Mumbai Central highlighted. Shortfalls included toilets at 201 stations, urinals at 403, and water taps at 2,035. In response, Railways announced a Tank to Tap water filtration system at 20,000 locations, replacement of water tanks, centralized monitoring, and regular source/outlet testing. Publication date 2026-08-16.

article.articleHeadline: Is Australia at risk of a measles outbreak?
article.articleSummary: Measles remains a threat to Australia, which eliminated transmission in 2014 but may face import-linked cases. About 1.7 million Australians may lack full protection, with roughly 7% inadequately immunized. At-risk groups include babies too young for vaccination and several older cohorts, notably those born around 1993–1995, 2000, and during vaccine rollout years 1977–1983. More than 100 measles cases have been recorded in 2026. The biggest risk is international travel and crowded airports rather than sustained community transmission. Vaccination is free via the National Immunisation Program at 12 and 18 months; catch-up doses are free for those under 20 who missed childhood vaccination. Adults may pay for vaccines, particularly for overseas travel. Regions abroad with outbreaks include the United States and Mexico; measles remains common in Bali, the Philippines and Vietnam. Health officials urge vaccination and travel consultation.

The case fatality rate among confirmed cases rose from about 20% in early June to 46% recently, though experts caution this reflects gaps in surveillance and access to care rather than increased virulence. article.articleHeadline: Middlesex County Resident Tests Positive for Zika Virus, First NJ Case in Six Years
article.articleSummary: Middlesex County resident diagnosed with travel-associated Zika virus; first New Jersey case since 2020, per the NJ Department of Health. Infection acquired abroad; destination and town undisclosed. Local risk remains extremely low; no continental U.S. transmission since 2018. Six travel-associated Zika diagnoses have been reported nationwide this year (CDC). Zika spreads primarily via Aedes aegypti bites, active after sunrise and around sunset; sexual and mother-to-fetus transmission are possible. Most infections are asymptomatic; about 20% develop fever, rash, red eyes, and joint or muscle pain lasting 2–7 days. Pregnancy poses higher risk; about 1 in 20 symptomatic pregnancies lead to congenital Zika syndrome (birth defects such as abnormal brain development, reduced head size, hearing loss, seizures). No vaccine or specific treatment; prevention focuses on mosquito bite avoidance and EPA-registered repellents. Updated data are available on the Vector-Borne Disease Data Dashboard; the 2015–2016 Brazil outbreak was the peak, with over 30,000 locally acquired U.S. cases, mostly in Puerto Rico.

article.articleHeadline: CAG Flags E Coli in Railway Station Water, Gaps in Passenger Amenities
article.articleSummary: Eight stations across four zones tested positive for E. coli in drinking-water sourced from water coolers: Coimbatore, Palakkad Junction; Hyderabad; CSMT Mumbai, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala; Madhupur. Tap water samples showed total coliforms across 49 stations in 2022-23 and 56 stations in 2023-24. Of 512 stations audited, 458 were deficient in Minimum Essential Amenities (MEAs) such as drinking water, toilets, seating, platform shelters, fans, water coolers and signage; only 54 had no shortfalls. Drinking-water booths unhygienic at 128 stations; platforms unclean at 77; stray dogs at 301. Even high-revenue NSG-1 to NSG-3 stations showed deficits; 10 high-earning stations had MEA gaps. Water taps missing or non-compliant at 138 stations. Railways ordered filtration systems at nearly 20,000 locations, tank replacements, regular testing and centralized monitoring; Amrit Bharat Scheme covers 325 non-Amrit Bharat stations amid modernization of over 1,300 stations since 2022.

article.articleHeadline: Cebu PVO brings rabies vaccination to 986 barangays
article.articleSummary: Cebu Province, Philippines, expanded rabies prevention to 986 barangays, with 51 local government units covered from July 2025 to July 2026. The Cebu Provincial Veterinary Office vaccinated 104,864 dogs and cats, distributed 31,667 vials of rabies vaccine, and served 103,296 clients, while conducting 5,264 spay/neuter procedures to manage animal populations. The effort is part of a provincial program on rabies prevention and animal population control, in collaboration with the Provincial Health Office on road safety and responsible pet ownership. Rabies remains a major public health concern in the Philippines; the DOH recorded 426 rabies-related deaths in 2024, and WHO deems mass dog vaccination the most cost-effective prevention since dogs account for up to 99% of human transmissions. Authorities urge owners to vaccinate, register, and prevent roaming animals, with teams moving quietly from barangay to barangay.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dangerous case of Japanese encephalitis virus infection reported.
article.articleSummary: On 17 August 2026, a 9-year-old girl from Lao Cai Province, Vietnam, developed Japanese encephalitis virus infection, initially presenting with fever and headache before rapidly progressing to coma and respiratory failure. She was transferred from a district hospital to the National Institute of Infectious Diseases in Hanoi. After two weeks of treatment, her consciousness improved and she could breathe independently, but she remains weak with ongoing risk of neurologic sequelae such as epilepsy and long-term impairment. The illness often begins with non-specific symptoms, making early recognition challenging, especially in young children who may cry or feed poorly. There is no specific antiviral therapy; care is supportive, focused on reducing brain edema, preventing seizures, and promptly addressing complications. Authorities report multiple pediatric JEV admissions recently and emphasize full vaccination and mosquito-control measures to prevent transmission.

Declared May 15, it is Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak and has accelerated amid weak health infrastructure, community resistance, and instability that hinder surveillance and case detection. The outbreak has no approved vaccines or treatments for Bundibugyo. It has spread to Uganda, where authorities limited deaths to two and confirmed 20 cases before declaring an end there last month. West Africa's 2014-2016 outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding.

Symptoms include hemorrhagic fever; there is no vaccine or targeted treatment for Bundibugyo in this outbreak in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes deadliest on record as death toll surpasses 2,300
article.articleSummary: As of 17 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing its deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, with 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths since it was declared on 15 May. The case fatality rate stands at 47%. The outbreak spans 55 health zones across six provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, South Kivu, and Bas-Uele. The Bundibugyo species has been identified as the cause. This surge surpasses the prior DR Congo outbreak (2018–2020) and marks the nation’s 17th Ebola epidemic since 1976. The World Health Organization warns the situation is evolving rapidly and calls for continued vigilance and a coordinated international response. If trends continue, the outbreak could exceed even the 2014–2016 West African outbreak, which infected over 28,600 people.

article.articleHeadline: Vì sao người cao tuổi dễ biến chứng do cúm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why are the elderly more susceptible to complications from influenza?
article.articleSummary: Influenza poses greater danger to the elderly, a high-risk group due to aging and chronic disease. In a case at the National Hospital of Tropical Diseases, a 77-year-old woman with hypertension developed influenza B–associated pneumonia requiring oxygen after four days of fatigue. Influenza markedly raises cardiovascular risk and death: myocardial infarction 6–10× higher and stroke ~8×; diabetics have hospitalization risk up sixfold and mortality two- to threefold. The elderly recover slowly, prolonging hospital stays; severe cases may require weeks in intensive care, mechanical ventilation, dialysis, or ECMO. Delayed care and self-medication are common, with antibiotics or corticosteroids often misused for a viral illness. Alarm signs include persistent high fever after 48 hours, chest tightness, dyspnea, rapid breathing, vomiting, or confusion. Vaccination, hygiene, and prompt evaluation are essential; healthy family members should vaccinate to reduce transmission, especially during travel seasons.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya tests 196 suspected Ebola cases, all return negative
article.articleSummary: Kenya reports 196 suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases tested negative as of August 16, 2026, with samples analyzed at the National Virology Reference Laboratory and partner labs; authorities continue surveillance to prevent spread. In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the Bundibugyo EVD outbreak declared May 15 has killed 2,184 and surpassed 4,660 cases, concentrated in Ituri Province (over 3,400) with affected areas in North Kivu and South Kivu; Uganda has reported 20 cases, signaling regional risk. The UN warns humanitarian and health systems are strained and has added $30.5 million from CERF, on top of $24 million previously released (about $54.5 million total). WFP reports over 260,000 hot meals at treatment and isolation centres in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu. The UN calls for scaling up: more safe/dignified burials teams, expanded treatment capacity, better contact tracing, and strengthened leadership amid ongoing conflict and malnutrition affecting roughly 2.6 million people in eastern DRC.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in country's history as death toll tops 2,300
article.articleSummary: DRC's current Ebola outbreak, declared May 15, is the deadliest in the country's history, with 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths (case fatality rate 47.0%). It spans 55 health zones across six provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uele. This is the DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak since 1976 and is caused by Bundibugyo virus. The World Health Organization warns it could be the worst on record; Tedros says it is moving faster and could eclipse the West Africa epidemic of 2014–2016, which infected more than 28,600 people. By comparison, the 2018–2020 eastern DRC outbreak had 3,481 cases and 2,299 deaths. Officials continue monitoring transmission and response efforts as the outbreak endures.

article.articleSummary: As of August 17, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed 2,325 lives among 4,945 confirmed cases over just under three months. article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri province, Bunia). As of 2026-08-17, 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths (case fatality ~46%), the DRC’s deadliest Ebola outbreak and the second-largest globally since 2014–2016. article.articleHeadline: 1.7 million Australians are not protected against measles... Is someone you know one of them?
article.articleSummary: As of 17 August 2026, Australia has about 1.7 million people susceptible to measles, with overall immunity at 93.3%—just at the WHO herd-immunity threshold (93–95%), based on 2019 data. The National Centre for Immunisation Research and Surveillance study—merging serology with vaccination records—identifies elevated vulnerability among infants, young children (not routinely vaccinated until 12 months), and adults aged 25–26, 31–33, and 42–49. Historical changes in immunisation, including the second-dose introduction and periods with only one dose or none, contribute to gaps. Measles is highly contagious: one infectious person can spread to 12–15 others; symptoms include fever, cough, red eyes, and a blotchy rash, with pneumonia or encephalitis possible. Australia eliminated measles in 2014, but imported cases have risen in the past two years as childhood vaccination coverage declined for a fifth year. Travellers are urged to verify two-dose vaccination; adults 20–40 linked to travel in Asia (Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand) may consider an extra dose.

article.articleHeadline: E. coli detected in drinking water at railway stations: CAG
article.articleSummary: E. coli detected in drinking water at Indian Railways stations across SR (Coimbatore, Palakkad Junctions), SCR (Hyderabad), CR (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan, Lonavala), and ER (Madhupur). Water coolers at these stations tested positive for E. coli; taps on platforms at 49 stations in eight zones during 2022-23 and 56 stations in nine zones during 2023-24 showed total coliform bacteria including E. coli. Some strains can cause food poisoning, diarrhoea and kidney failure. Bacteriological tests beyond total coliforms were unsatisfactory at eight stations in four zones (2022-23) and 11 stations in five zones (2023-24). The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit spans 2019-20 to 2023-24, with earlier unreported cases; Indian Railways NSG comprises 5,908 stations, over 7,424 daily non-suburban trains, and 292.4 crore non-suburban passengers in 2023-24. The audit assessed sanitation and passenger amenities against Railway Board guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses Previous Record, Becomes Deadliest in Nation's History
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, now the deadliest in the nation's history, has 4,945 infections and 2,325 deaths, with 101 new cases in the last 24 hours. It is the DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak and has surpassed the 2018–2020 toll. The case fatality ratio has climbed from about 20% in early June to roughly 46%, likely due to late detection and deaths in communities before care. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments. Contributing factors include weak health infrastructure, remoteness, and ongoing conflict near borders with South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda, hindering response. WHO Director-General Tedros warned the outbreak could outpace the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Health authorities are evaluating experimental vaccines and therapies; evidence is mostly limited to animal studies, with emphasis on contact tracing and early detection.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills 2,325, becoming deadliest in country's history
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the deadliest in the country’s history, with 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths since the current outbreak began, a case fatality rate of 47.0%. The latest figures come from a situation report released by the DRC health authorities and reflect the situation as of 2026-08-17. The toll surpasses the 2018-2020 Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC, which the World Health Organization recorded at 3,481 cases and 2,299 deaths. The article notes the outbreak is ongoing but provides no start date or additional clinical details beyond the counts and fatalities.

article.articleHeadline: RDC/Ebola : l'épidémie devient la plus meurtrière de l'histoire du pays avec plus de 2.300 morts
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC/Ebola: the outbreak becomes the deadliest in the country's history with more than 2,300 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo becomes the deadliest in the country’s history, with more than 2,300 deaths. As of 16 August 2026, the outbreak has 4,945 confirmed cases, 2,325 deaths (case fatality rate 47%), and 1,040 recoveries. Declared 15 May, it is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC since 1976 and is caused by the Bundibugyo strain. It now spans 55 health zones across six provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu, and Bas-Uélé. The outbreak is already the second largest on record and is advancing faster than earlier ones; at the current pace, it could surpass West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic, which infected more than 28,600 people, according to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.
